title: When the Choir Breaks
premise: In the city of Vellamere, where magic is outlawed and beasts are silenced, Casper Hartwell hides his gift of hearing and speaking with animals behind a shopfront of harmless charms. When a dying stranger presses a bloodstained map into his hands, Casper learns the king has been hollowed out by a memory-eating entity called the Chorister, which sustains itself by stealing the identities of the gifted. Guided by the map and a sarcastic one-eyed crow named Bramble, Casper must reach the palace vaults and sing the counter-song that can unbind the king before the Chorister consumes the last of his memories. In the climax, Casper offers his own most precious memories as bait, nearly losing himself, but the freed king's restored voice joins his to shatter the Chorister's chorus. Casper survives diminished but whole, and in a city where magic is no longer feared into silence, he finally belongs.
about_author: Lena Marchetti spent her childhood on a coastal farm where she claims she learned to argue with gulls. She now writes fantasy about outsiders, animal whisperers, and the quiet cost of belonging from a cluttered studio overlooking the sea.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Five years after fleeing persecution, Casper sells counterfeit charms in Vellamere while secretly conversing with rats and pigeons who warn him of wardens. A bleeding stranger staggers into his shop, presses a map into his hands, and dies whispering that 'the crown is singing.' Casper wants only to burn the map, but the city's beasts beg him not to. Emotional beat: fear of exposure warring with a buried longing to matter.

chapters.title: What the Crows Remember
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with interludes from Bramble the crow. Following the map through the flooded undercity, Casper discovers the stranger was a court beast-speaker who uncovered the Chorister's existence. Wardens ambush them; Casper must use his gift openly for the first time, commanding a swarm of rats to escape. He learns the Chorister eats memories and identity, leaving its victims smiling and empty. Emotional beat: terror transforming into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Disguised as a palace lamplighter, Casper reaches the throne room and finds the king a puppet—his memories siphoned nightly by the Chorister, a radiant thing woven from stolen voices. Captured by the queen, herself half-consumed, Casper bargains: his rare gift can enter the song where ordinary magic cannot. The Chorister begins pulling at his memories of his mother. Emotional beat: dread and grief as Casper realizes the price of the counter-song.

chapters.title: A Voice Returned
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, Casper's POV. In the vaults, Casper sings the counter-song, feeding the Chorister his dearest memories as bait until he barely knows his own name. The king, reawakened by fragments Casper returns to him, joins the song; their two voices crack the chorus and unmake the creature. Memories flood back to the city's emptied. Weeks later, magic is decriminalized, and Casper—missing some things but certain of who he is—opens his shop door to the first students of a new choir. Emotional beat: loss transmuted into belonging.
